item.title: Praise and criticism
item.description: Precise words for judging work, ideas and performances.

children.definition: extremely critical in an angry or scornful way
children.example: The novel received a scathing review in a national newspaper.
The proposal met with a lukewarm response from the board.

children.definition: deserving praise, even if not fully successful
children.example: Their aim is laudable, but the plan is unrealistic.

children.definition: having a mistake or weakness that makes it less effective or valid
children.example: The study was deeply flawed because the sample was too small.

children.definition: copying the ideas of others; not original
children.example: Critics found the film derivative and predictable.

children.definition: showing clear thought and the ability to get to the heart of an issue
children.example: Her incisive questions exposed the weaknesses in the argument.
The writing is competent but rather pedestrian.

children.definition: very important and strongly influencing later work
children.example: Her seminal paper changed the way linguists study bilingual children.

children.definition: to speak about someone or something in a way that shows you do not respect them
children.example: He never disparages his rivals in public.

children.definition: strongly suggesting that someone is guilty or has done something wrong
children.example: The audit produced a damning report on the company's finances.

children.definition: pleasingly simple and not trying to attract attention
children.example: The hotel's design is elegant and understated.

children.definition: to praise someone or something so weakly that it sounds like criticism
children.example: Calling her speech 'adequate' was damning it with faint praise.
